The act of State doctrine denotes that the assessment as to the existence of an alleged tort committed by a State belongs to the executive and not the courts. Domestic courts treat a recognized foreign sovereign’s public acts within its own territory as valid and non-justiciable, and leave the matter to diplomacy and the executive’s conduct of foreign relations. That is the rule in Underhill v. Hernandez and Banco Nacional de Cuba v. Sabbatino, and in the related English doctrine of non-justiciability.
